root_cause.text: Missing l2cap_chan_lock acquisition before calling l2cap_chan_del() in l2cap_ecred_reconf_rsp(), allowing concurrent manipulation of the channel list without synchronization.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "l2cap_ecred_reconf_rsp() calls l2cap_chan_del() without holding l2cap_chan_lock(). Every other l2cap_chan_del() caller in the file acquires the lock first. A remote BLE device can send a crafted L2CAP ECRED reconfiguration response to corrupt the channel list while another thread is iterating it." The patch adds l2cap_chan_hold(), l2cap_chan_lock() before the del, and l2cap_chan_unlock(), l2cap_chan_put() after.

candidates.rationale: This condition controls which channel is selected for deletion; without proper locking, the channel list may be concurrently modified, leading to use of a stale or dangling pointer.
Skips remaining loop iteration for non-matching channels; part of the vulnerable logic that reaches the deletion without synchronization.
Directly deletes a channel without holding l2cap_chan_lock, allowing concurrent modification of the channel list and leading to use-after-free or list corruption.
Closing brace of the loop body; marks the end of the unprotected code section where synchronization is missing.
Function exit point; without lock protection, the return may occur while another thread is still manipulating the channel list, leading to inconsistent state.
